# Validation Evidence Matrix

<!-- Generated by docs/generate_validation_matrix.py; do not edit by hand. -->

This matrix distinguishes independent physical validation from regression
coverage. The authoritative records are in `validation/evidence.json`.
A passing test protects behavior; only the evidence levels below describe
what supports the underlying scientific or numerical claim.

## Evidence Levels

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **A** | Analytical identity, exact solution, or limiting case |
| **B** | Parity with the MATLAB or Octave reference implementation |
| **C** | Comparison with an independent numerical tool or implementation |
| **D** | Published benchmark, theory curve, or literature dataset |
| **E** | Comparison with experimental measurements |
| **R** | Regression, invariant, or internal cross-backend check |

## Detailed Evidence

### Bloch rotations and acquisition kernels

- **Claim:** Core rotations, echo conversion, acquisition, and arb10 propagation reproduce the established MATLAB/Octave implementation.
- **Evidence:** B, A (validated)
- **Basis:** CSV fixtures generated from MATLAB R2025b or Octave 11.3, plus rotation-matrix invariants.
- **Tested range:** Compact offset grids and ideal/tuned/untuned/matched reference parameter sets stored in validation/fixtures.
- **Metric:** Elementwise numerical agreement
- **Tolerance:** Per-test numpy.testing tolerances, normally 1e-10 to 1e-7 absolute/relative.
- **References:** MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/octave_fixtures/core.py::test_calc_rotation_matrix_matches_octave`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/octave_fixtures/core.py#L572); [`validation/octave/generate_basic_fixtures.m`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/validation/octave/generate_basic_fixtures.m)
- **Limitations:** Fixtures sample representative grids; they are not an exhaustive proof over all parameter combinations.

### CPMG, FID, imaging, and probe workflows

- **Claim:** Public ideal, tuned, untuned, and matched workflow assemblies preserve the reference signal and result conventions.
- **Evidence:** B, R (validated)
- **Basis:** MATLAB/Octave workflow fixtures, result-shape checks, and serial/parallel equality tests.
- **Tested range:** Representative finite/asymptotic echo trains, Q and mistuning sweeps, and compact imaging phantoms.
- **Metric:** Array agreement and workflow invariants
- **Tolerance:** Fixture-specific numerical tolerances; exact equality for deterministic serial/parallel paths.
- **References:** MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/octave_fixtures/workflows.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/octave_fixtures/workflows.py); [`validation/octave/generate_imaging_fixtures.m`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/validation/octave/generate_imaging_fixtures.m)
- **Limitations:** High-Q matched-probe coverage remains concentrated on compact fixtures.

### Probe pulse responses and phase programs

- **Claim:** Rectangular tuned, untuned, and matched pulse responses and selected phase-program helpers match the MATLAB implementation.
- **Evidence:** B (validated)
- **Basis:** MATLAB/Octave waveform and catalog fixtures.
- **Tested range:** Bundled rectangular-pulse fixtures and selected SPA phase programs.
- **Metric:** Complex waveform and scalar metric agreement
- **Tolerance:** Per-fixture numerical tolerances, normally near floating-point precision.
- **References:** MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code/Pulse Shape
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/octave_fixtures/optimization.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/octave_fixtures/optimization.py); [`validation/octave/generate_pulse_fixtures.m`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/validation/octave/generate_pulse_fixtures.m)
- **Limitations:** Arbitrary measured probe transfer functions are not covered by the historical fixtures.

### Sequence IR, Pulseq interchange, and compiler

- **Claim:** Core Pulseq 1.4/1.5 events retain timing and metadata through import, compilation, plotting data, facade execution, and raster-aligned 1.5.0 round trips.
- **Evidence:** R (regression only)
- **Basis:** Hand-audited Pulseq text fixtures, round-trip checks, exact timing assertions, moving-isochromat facade parity, and signature verification.
- **Tested range:** Core RF, arbitrary/trapezoid gradients, ADC, compressed shapes, offsets, and block timing.
- **Metric:** Exact metadata/timing invariants and numerical waveform equality
- **Tolerance:** Exact for discrete metadata; 1e-12 seconds or tighter for timing comparisons.
- **References:** Pulseq specification 1.4.x and 1.5.0
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_sequence_ir.py::test_imports_pulseq_15_rf_adc_and_compiles`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_sequence_ir.py#L215); [`tests/test_sequence_ir.py::test_round_trip_preserves_core_events_and_metadata`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_sequence_ir.py#L276); [`tests/test_sequence_ir.py::test_export_signature_covers_sequence_text`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_sequence_ir.py#L342); [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_sequence_ir_facade_matches_direct_motion_backend`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L1660); [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_sequence_ir_facade_executes_pulseq_round_trip`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L1741)
- **Limitations:** No independent scanner/vendor execution comparison yet. Optional extensions are retained but not executed.

### PGSE diffusion encoding

- **Claim:** The deterministic moment backend follows the Stejskal-Tanner b-value and exp(-bD) attenuation, and free walkers converge toward that result.
- **Evidence:** A, C (validated)
- **Basis:** Closed-form Stejskal-Tanner equations and an independently sampled random-walker backend.
- **Tested range:** Rectangular lobes, unrestricted isotropic diffusion, zero-gradient/diffusion limits, and compact walker ensembles.
- **Metric:** b-value equality, log-signal slope, and walker confidence envelope
- **Tolerance:** Machine precision for moments; statistical tolerance set from finite walker count for particle simulations.
- **References:** Stejskal-Tanner pulsed-gradient spin-echo theory
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_pgse.py::test_moment_b_value_matches_stejskal_tanner_formula`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_pgse.py#L65); [`tests/test_pgse.py::test_moment_signal_has_expected_diffusion_slope`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_pgse.py#L83); [`tests/test_pgse.py::test_walker_pgse_converges_toward_moment_attenuation`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_pgse.py#L128)
- **Limitations:** The analytical comparison assumes unrestricted isotropic diffusion and ideal rectangular gradients.

### Moving-isochromat diffusion and boundaries

- **Claim:** Seeded particle motion has the expected diffusion statistics, boundary behavior, RF rotation, and static-gradient refocusing limits.
- **Evidence:** A, R (validated)
- **Basis:** Brownian mean-square displacement, deterministic zero-diffusion limits, and sequence refocusing invariants.
- **Tested range:** One to three spatial dimensions with reflecting/periodic boundaries on sampled domains.
- **Metric:** Moment statistics, signal limits, and deterministic seed equality
- **Tolerance:** Analytical or sampling-error tolerance chosen per test.
- **References:** Brownian diffusion and spin-echo refocusing identities
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_motion.py::test_advection_diffusion_and_boundaries_are_seeded`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_motion.py#L126); [`tests/test_motion_sequence.py::test_cpmg_sequence_refocuses_static_gradient_without_diffusion`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_motion_sequence.py#L99)
- **Limitations:** Complex pore geometries have synthetic rather than experimental benchmarks.

### Flow washout and transit polarization

- **Claim:** Plug and laminar pipe washout and flux-weighted transit polarization follow their analytical distributions and Monte Carlo estimates.
- **Evidence:** A, C (validated)
- **Basis:** Closed-form residence-time distributions and independent Monte Carlo sampling.
- **Tested range:** Ideal plug and fully developed laminar flow in a cylindrical sensitive region.
- **Metric:** Survival fraction, density normalization, mean transit time, and polarization
- **Tolerance:** Exact/near-machine precision for identities; finite-sample bounds for Monte Carlo checks.
- **References:** Poiseuille flow and flux-weighted residence-time theory
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_flow.py::test_laminar_matches_derived_piecewise`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_flow.py#L60); [`tests/test_flow.py::test_monte_carlo_cross_check_laminar`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_flow.py#L109); [`tests/test_flow.py::test_monte_carlo_flux_weighted_cross_check`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_flow.py#L242)
- **Limitations:** No CFD or turbulent-flow comparison; velocity profiles are prescribed.

### Magnetostatic field solvers

- **Claim:** Biot-Savart coil fields and selected magnet geometries reproduce analytical center-field, symmetry, scaling, finite-length, and far-field limits; the documented AlNiCo electropermanent rod also reproduces its published surface-field benchmark.
- **Evidence:** A, D (validated)
- **Basis:** Circular-loop center field, symmetry planes, current scaling, known Halbach field orientation, exact finite-cylinder axial fields, point-dipole limits, and a published AlNiCo-5 rod benchmark.
- **Tested range:** Loop coils, yoke-image checks, finite Halbach rods, NMR-MOUSE-scale grids, and finite cylindrical AlNiCo rods and bundles.
- **Metric:** Vector-field value, direction, symmetry, and scaling
- **Tolerance:** Geometry/discretization-specific tolerances declared in tests.
- **References:** Biot-Savart circular-loop solution; Ideal Halbach dipole symmetry; Weinberg Medical Physics variable-field NMR AlNiCo rod measurements
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_magnetostatics.py::test_loop_center_matches_analytic`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_magnetostatics.py#L27); [`tests/test_magnetostatics.py::test_field_scales_with_current`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_magnetostatics.py#L36); [`tests/test_magnetostatics.py::test_four_rod_halbach_phasing_points_bore_field_along_x`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_magnetostatics.py#L105); [`tests/test_electropermanent.py::test_published_rod_matches_reported_surface_field_scale`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent.py#L53); [`tests/test_electropermanent.py::test_cubature_converges_to_exact_on_axis_cylinder_field`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent.py#L63); [`tests/test_electropermanent.py::test_far_field_matches_magnetic_dipole_limit`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent.py#L88)
- **Limitations:** Static field evaluation consumes a retained state supplied directly or by a programming model; quasistatic self-demagnetizing and neighbor coupling are handled by the separate coupled programmer rather than the field evaluator itself.

### Electropermanent programming pulses and retained state

- **Claim:** The NumPy capacitor/H-bridge/series-RLC integrator reproduces the exact underdamped current solution and configuration-specific fits recover the archived 220/400/600-V peak-current examples; empirical remanence updates enforce their calibrated branch, polarity, range, uncertainty, and provenance.
- **Evidence:** A, E, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Exact underdamped series-RLC current, electrical energy balance, archived peak-current traces, and protocol invariants for the coarse published demagnetization envelope.
- **Tested range:** 10--50 us gates, 220--600 V capacitor commands, approximately 147--330 A measured peaks, passive recovery, and a 0--100 percent saturate-then-demagnetize command.
- **Metric:** Current waveform and peak, energy residual, temperature direction, retained remanence, branch, reversal point, and uncertainty
- **Tolerance:** 2e-8 relative for the analytical RLC waveform; 4 percent for configuration-specific archived peak-current fits; exact protocol guards and interpolation anchors.
- **References:** Weinberg archive MRI/IGBT_board/experimental results.pdf; Weinberg archive NQR_proposal_2019 demagnetization figure; Series-RLC transient solution
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py::test_drive_matches_exact_underdamped_series_rlc_current`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py#L48); [`tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py::test_archived_peak_current_cases_match_configuration_specific_fits`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py#L149); [`tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py::test_recovery_path_decays_current_and_closes_energy_balance`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py#L91); [`tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py::test_published_protocol_zero_crossing_updates_state_and_history`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_pulses.py#L213)
- **Limitations:** Effective L/R/C values are inferred fits rather than independently measured parameters for every trace; the three-anchor remanence envelope is not raw hysteresis data and cannot predict arbitrary minor loops. The separate return-point model is currently illustrative rather than measured.

### Electropermanent return-point memory and neighbor coupling

- **Claim:** Weighted play operators close nested reversal loops exactly and obey wiping-out, while finite-geometry two-element coupling has the expected symmetry and sign and the self-demagnetizing programming fixed point converges.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Scalar play-operator return-point identities, finite-magnet dipole symmetry, and explicit fixed-point residual checks.
- **Tested range:** Illustrative six-operator AlNiCo model over plus/minus 400 kA/m, side-by-side finite rods, optional diagonal demagnetizing factors, and one programmed target per solve.
- **Metric:** Loop-closure error, retained remanence, coupling-matrix sign and symmetry, iteration count, and fixed-point residual
- **Tolerance:** Machine precision for exact nested-loop closure; geometry-specific symmetry tolerances and 1 uT retained-remanence convergence in regression tests.
- **References:** Scalar play-operator hysteresis and return-point memory; Finite magnetic-dipole interaction symmetry
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py::test_return_to_nested_reversal_restores_operator_state_exactly`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py#L43); [`tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py::test_exceeding_outer_return_point_wipes_inner_memory`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py#L62); [`tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py::test_geometry_coupling_is_symmetric_and_equatorial_field_is_opposed`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py#L140); [`tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py::test_saturated_neighbor_changes_partial_programming_result`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py#L153); [`tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py::test_self_demagnetizing_fixed_point_converges`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_hysteresis.py#L209)
- **Limitations:** The bundled thresholds, weights, saturation remanence, and temperature coefficient are illustrative inferred values rather than a measured AlNiCo minor-loop fit; transient winding interaction is handled by a separate multi-channel model whose coupling matrices require measurement.

### Electropermanent transient winding cross-talk

- **Claim:** The multi-winding integrator reduces to the isolated RLC driver at zero coupling, produces the Lenz-law neighbor-current sign for positive mutual inductance, closes the coupled electrical-energy balance, and propagates pulse-driven disturbance into every return-point state.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Zero-coupling reduction, initial coupled-inductor derivative sign, capacitor plus coupled-inductor energy conservation with resistive loss, and synthetic threshold-crossing regressions.
- **Tested range:** Two closed recovery windings, dimensionless mutual coefficients through 0.15, 20--30 us gates, 50--100 V commands, winding leakage through 0.20, and state-dependent self inductance through 25 percent.
- **Metric:** Current and induced-voltage sign, waveform deviation from isolated drive, energy residual, internal field, retained-state change, and fixed-point residual
- **Tolerance:** 2e-12 waveform reduction tolerance, 0.02 percent relative energy residual, exact sign/threshold checks, and 2 uT retained-state convergence.
- **References:** Coupled-inductor circuit equations and Lenz's law; Weinberg archive 20200525 IGBT update neighbor-effect observations
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py::test_zero_coupling_reproduces_isolated_target_waveform`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py#L71); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py::test_positive_mutual_inductance_opposes_neighbor_current_ramp`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py#L98); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py::test_coupled_circuit_closes_electrical_energy_balance`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py#L117); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py::test_transient_crosstalk_disturbs_neighbor_return_point_state`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py#L194); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py::test_state_dependent_inductance_outer_iteration_converges`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transient.py#L209)
- **Limitations:** Inactive channels are modeled as closed through recovery resistors; open, actively clamped, and multiplexed topologies are not yet available. Mutual inductance and winding-field leakage are explicit inferred inputs because no measured array matrix is bundled.

### Hybrid electropermanent array and operating-state synthesis

- **Claim:** The cached fixed-plus-programmable field basis exactly reproduces direct finite-magnet superposition, and bounded synthesis recovers representable targets while reducing the reference field-off residual and preserving a requested transport-gradient sign.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Linearity of magnetostatic fields in retained remanence, direct-versus-cached finite-rod field comparison, exact synthetic bounded least squares, and full 18-sub-unit array regressions.
- **Tested range:** Two illustrative opposing 3-by-3 panels with 18 hybrid sub-units, 72 AlNiCo controls, retained-remanence limits of plus/minus 0.33 T, compact control-region samples, uniform imaging and field-off targets, and affine transport gradients.
- **Metric:** Vector-field equality, target residual, reference-to-field-off RMS reduction, retained-state bounds, saturation count, and fitted centerline gradient sign
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point equality for cached/direct superposition and representable synthetic targets; geometry-specific reduction and gradient-sign checks for the illustrative full array.
- **References:** Magnetostatic superposition and linearity in magnetization; Weinberg project evidence for the 18-sub-unit, 72-control hierarchy and control-region intent
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_array.py::test_cached_basis_matches_direct_superposition`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_array.py#L45); [`tests/test_electropermanent_array.py::test_numpy_bounded_solver_recovers_representable_target`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_array.py#L90); [`tests/test_electropermanent_array.py::test_field_off_synthesis_reduces_reference_array_field`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_array.py#L106); [`tests/test_electropermanent_array.py::test_transport_target_and_synthesis_preserve_gradient_direction`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_array.py#L131); [`examples/plot_epm_hybrid_array_synthesis.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_hybrid_array_synthesis.py)
- **Limitations:** The exact historical rod dimensions, pitch, and within-sub-unit layout are inferred illustrative assumptions until CAD or measured field bases are available. Transport synthesis targets an affine projected static field; particle dynamics are tracked by a separate validation record, while programming schedules and closed-loop control are not yet included. Nonlinear imaging is also tracked separately.

### Nonlinear electropermanent-array imaging

- **Claim:** Retained-state fields generate the expected receiver-demodulated phase matrix, and nonnegative regularized inversion reproducibly reconstructs a noisy two-tissue phantom while localizing its off-center target.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Direct cached-field evaluation, the analytical phase relation gamma times encoding duration times field offset, seeded complex-noise regression, and a known synthetic proton-density/T1/T2 phantom.
- **Tested range:** Illustrative 18-sub-unit/72-control array, 10-by-10 through 16-by-16 Cartesian tissue phantoms over 40 mm, 160 through 384 retained-state acquisitions, 250--300 us phase encoding, and 35 dB RMS acquisition SNR.
- **Metric:** Field and phase equality, matrix magnitude, inverse-system condition number, image NRMSE, convergence, repeatability, and target-centroid error
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point field/phase identities; below 3 percent NRMSE and condition number below 10 for the compact seeded regression.
- **References:** General spatial encoding matrix s_k = sum_j rho_j exp(-i phi_kj); Known synthetic tissue phantom generated by the package
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_imaging.py::test_encoding_matches_cached_fields_and_reference_demodulation`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_imaging.py#L56); [`tests/test_electropermanent_imaging.py::test_noisy_tissue_reconstruction_is_reproducible_and_accurate`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_imaging.py#L81); [`examples/plot_epm_nonlinear_tissue_imaging.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_nonlinear_tissue_imaging.py)
- **Limitations:** Tissue relaxation constants, encoding states, array geometry, and noise are illustrative rather than measured platform data. The workflow models one static phase-encoding interval per retained state and a real nonnegative spin-echo image; RF excitation, EPM programming time, eddy-current transients, off-resonance relaxation during readout, and multi-coil sensitivity encoding are not yet coupled. Synthetic reconstruction validates the implemented inverse but is not an independent experimental or scanner benchmark.

### Susceptibility-aware EPM particle MR sequence comparison

- **Claim:** A selected retained EPM state supplies the background B0 map; field-dependent equivalent-sphere particle moments generate subvoxel dipole perturbations while magnetic-core samples exclude water signal; paired finite-pulse spin echo, Cartesian GRE, GRE phase-gradient mapping, and center-out radial short-TE acquisitions propagate tissue relaxation and diffusing water; and reference-supported contrast yields image-derived susceptibility foci and centroids without reading particle truth.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Uniformly magnetized sphere interior and exterior dipole identities, direct EPM field-basis evaluation, explicit finite-pulse spin echo and GRE propagation, paired complex phase derivatives, center-out non-Cartesian encoding, paired seeded random-walker diffusion, and synthetic contrast-localization fixtures.
- **Tested range:** Two-dimensional uniform Cartesian tissue maps; one through nine subvoxel samples per axis; non-negative water diffusion; one or more walkers per voxel; linear or Langevin particle magnetization; finite excitation, refocusing, phase-encoding, Cartesian-readout, and radial-readout durations; optional per-acquisition relative complex noise.
- **Metric:** Dipole-field sign and symmetry, nonzero particle delta B0, selected EPM background field, spatial subvoxel propagation, center-k-space time, resolved contrast foci, centroid error, symmetric nearest-focus error, controller consumption of the reconstructed outside-target centroid, and seeded repeatability.
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point dipole symmetry identities; exact configuration and seeded-output identities; positive physical contrast in the compact regression; centroid error is reported because blooming depends strongly on size, field, sequence, and resolution.
- **References:** Mani et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 55 (2006), 126-135, DOI 10.1002/mrm.20739; Zhao et al., NMR in Biomedicine 24 (2011), 464-472, DOI 10.1002/nbm.1608; Gharagouzloo et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 74 (2015), 431-441, DOI 10.1002/mrm.25426
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_equivalent_sphere_field_has_expected_axial_and_equatorial_signs`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L116); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_contrast_estimator_returns_resolved_foci_without_particle_truth`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L132); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_spin_echo_uses_epm_b0_and_particle_subvoxel_field`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L151); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_gre_ute_and_phase_gradient_share_physical_particle_model`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L194); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_controller_can_use_phase_gradient_susceptibility_feedback`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L338); [`tests/test_imaging_frequency.py::test_gradient_echo_localizes_a_point_without_refocusing`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_imaging_frequency.py#L62); [`tests/test_imaging_frequency.py::test_radial_ute_localizes_a_point_at_short_echo_time`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_imaging_frequency.py#L72); [`examples/plot_epm_particle_spin_echo.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_particle_spin_echo.py); [`examples/plot_epm_particle_sequence_comparison.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_particle_sequence_comparison.py)
- **Limitations:** The equivalent-sphere field does not yet model rod orientation, nonspherical demagnetization, particle-particle magnetic interaction, aggregation-dependent magnetization, or microscopic water exchange. The acquisition engines model a two-dimensional slice with ideal rectangular RF drive, scalar B1 maps, Cartesian or ideal center-out gradients, and a mesoscopic subvoxel/random-walker approximation; they are not scanner-validated Bloch-Torrey calculations. The radial short-TE path does not infer concentration-dependent T1 relaxivity or steady-state saturation, and optional SNR is relative per acquisition rather than bandwidth- and scan-time-matched absolute noise. Target contrast fraction is not particle occupancy or particle count. Static spin echo suppresses susceptibility sensitivity, while finite-bandwidth, phase-gradient, radial-undersampling, and readout effects cause blooming or artifact foci and can shift the recovered centroid. The example uses an illustrative 100 um effective magnetic core and disables receiver noise by default to isolate sequence physics; it is not an injectable-particle detectability claim.

### Image-guided superparamagnetic particle transport

- **Claim:** The transport workflow recovers the analytical linear superparamagnetic force and Stokes--Einstein limits, smoothly caps magnetization with a Langevin law, differentiates affine fields correctly, and reproducibly integrates seeded flow/diffusion trajectories with target capture.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Closed-form force, Stokes drag, Stokes--Einstein diffusion, and affine-field gradient identities plus seeded synthetic trajectory regressions coupled to the known tissue phantom.
- **Tested range:** Two-dimensional sampled vector fields; positive SI particle radii, viscosity, temperature, and saturation magnetization; non-negative susceptibility; linear and Langevin magnetization; rectangular reflect, periodic, and clip boundaries; constant, array, or callable background velocities.
- **Metric:** Force vector, magnetization limit, diffusion coefficient, grad(|B|^2), trajectory repeatability, cumulative capture monotonicity, peak force, and capture fraction
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point analytical identities; seeded trajectory equality; qualitative positive capture in the compact regression.
- **References:** Linear superparamagnetic force F = V chi grad(|B|^2)/(2 mu0); Langevin magnetization, Stokes drag, and Stokes--Einstein diffusion
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_stokes_einstein_diffusion_and_drag_are_consistent`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L28); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_langevin_force_recovers_linear_low_field_and_saturates`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L36); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_linear_force_matches_closed_form_identity`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L57); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_force_map_recovers_affine_field_gradient`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L84); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_seeded_transport_is_reproducible_and_captures_target`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L103); [`examples/plot_epm_image_guided_transport.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_image_guided_transport.py)
- **Limitations:** The integrated example uses an illustrative 30 um hydrodynamic magnetic aggregate and inferred array geometry, not a calibrated nanoparticle formulation or clinical dose. The first transport model is dilute and overdamped; it omits particle-particle interactions, aggregation kinetics, adhesion and release kinetics, branching vasculature, porous tissue permeability, hydrodynamic wall corrections, and feedback on field or flow. Target capture is irreversible on entry to a circle. The alternating controller is tracked by a separate validation record.

### Alternating image-guided EPM therapy controller

- **Claim:** The controller executes contiguous image-program-transport-verification intervals, supports the calibrated direct-signal baseline and selectable susceptibility-aware spin echo, GRE, GRE phase-gradient, or radial short-TE acquisition, re-aims each affine transport objective from the reconstructed outside-target centroid, and stops reproducibly from verification imaging rather than simulator truth.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Cloud-in-cell conservation identities, exact noiseless image-state recovery cases, state-machine interval identities, direct estimated-centroid direction geometry, seeded noisy nonlinear reconstructions and Brownian paths, retained-state total variation, and persistent-capture regressions.
- **Tested range:** One through four cycles in compact regressions and examples; 5-by-5 estimator identity grids and 10-by-10 through 20-by-20 EPM encoding/force grids; 3 through 80 illustrative magnetic aggregates; configurable target, particle, and verification imaging noise/regularization, signal per particle, support threshold, boundary-capture partial-volume correction, timing windows, and capture goals in (0, 1].
- **Metric:** Deposited signal and first moment, recovered count and representative positions, target and particle centroids, occupancy, centroid/occupancy error against hidden truth, mode order and contiguity, requested direction, remanence variation, force, stopping reason, and seeded repeatability
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point deposition, centroid, interval, and direction identities; exact noiseless count/occupancy fixtures; exact seeded output equality; image-derived configured stopping semantics; noisy estimator error is reported rather than hidden by a fixed acceptance claim.
- **References:** Cloud-in-cell concentration imaging and image-moment identities; Feedback state-machine and centroid steering identities; Package nonlinear EPM imaging and magnetophoretic transport validation records
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_peak_relative_localization_returns_weighted_centroid`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L27); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_cloud_in_cell_image_preserves_count_and_centroid`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L48); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_image_estimator_recovers_count_positions_centroid_and_occupancy`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L65); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_boundary_capture_correction_uses_grid_geometry_not_particle_truth`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L85); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_noisy_particle_imaging_is_reproducible_and_image_resolved`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L300); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_controller_can_use_phase_gradient_susceptibility_feedback`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L338); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_controller_alternates_modes_reaims_and_accumulates_capture`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L390); [`tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py::test_seeded_controller_is_reproducible`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_controller.py#L427); [`tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py::test_initial_capture_mask_keeps_particles_immobilized`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_transport.py#L159); [`examples/plot_epm_closed_loop_controller.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_closed_loop_controller.py)
- **Limitations:** The direct-signal baseline uses a supplied signal per aggregate and is not a physical MR contrast mechanism. The susceptibility options are physical but uncalibrated and their target contrast fraction is not a particle count or occupancy measurement. Recovered positions are representative image-resolved distribution samples or susceptibility foci, not identity-preserving tracks. The direct-channel boundary-capture partial-volume correction follows from the simulated first-entry capture rule and grid geometry; it requires experimental validation and does not apply to blooming physical contrast. Summed retained-remanence variation is a programming-effort metric, not pulse count, switching energy, temperature, or driver stress. A calibrated 72-channel programming schedule is required for those quantities. The controller inherits the illustrative array, aggregate, dilute transport, irreversible circular capture, and missing vascular/tissue physics of the component models.

### Dynamic-inversion ferromagnetic-particle trap

- **Claim:** The workflow executes the published polarize-delay-antialigned-gradient timing, recovers spherical Stokes and Tirado finite-cylinder diffusion limits, reproducibly couples rigid-body and magnetic-moment orientation to translation, distinguishes contraction from rapidly relaxing-moment expansion, and makes coil, EPM-only, and hybrid switching burdens explicit.
- **Evidence:** A, D, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Closed-form Stokes and rotational Einstein limits, the two-dimensional polar-orientation correlation exp(-D_r*t), published Tirado finite-cylinder diffusion expressions, the Nacev 2015 pulse order and timing, seeded stochastic trajectory regression, and exact architecture pulse-count identities.
- **Tested range:** Two-dimensional dilute particles represented as spheres or rods with rod aspect ratio at least 2; rigid or finite internal moment relaxation; four-direction inverse-power source model; configurable polarizer, gradient, geometry, flow, Brownian motion, reflecting bounds, timing, EPM parallelism, and optional calibrated pulse energies.
- **Metric:** Translational and rotational drag/diffusion, deterministic and Brownian-limited effective orientation-memory time, repulsive gradient fraction, RMS-radius concentration gain, target retention and escape, seeded repeatability, state/channel pulse count, timing margin, waveform fidelity, and average power when energy inputs are supplied
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point analytical drag/diffusion and two-dimensional polar-correlation identities; exact seeded trajectory equality; qualitative contraction for the compact rigid long-rod case and expansion for its 100 ns internal-relaxation control; exact integer hardware counts and a Brownian-dominated infeasibility regression.
- **References:** Nacev et al., Nano Letters 15 (2015), 359-364, DOI 10.1021/nl503654t; Tirado, Martinez, and Garcia de la Torre, Journal of Chemical Physics 81 (1984), 2047-2052, DOI 10.1063/1.447827
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_sphere_drag_recovers_stokes_and_rotational_limits`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L37); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_brownian_orientation_correlation_matches_two_dimensional_sde`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L82); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_brownian_diffusion_limits_small_particle_hardware_feasibility`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L257); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_rod_diffusion_matches_tirado_finite_cylinder_expressions`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L62); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_seeded_dynamic_inversion_is_reproducible_and_nonsticky`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L110); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_rigid_long_rod_contracts_while_fast_moment_relaxation_expands`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L159); [`tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py::test_architecture_counts_and_waveform_consequences_are_explicit`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electropermanent_dynamic_inversion.py#L226); [`examples/plot_epm_dynamic_inversion.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_epm_dynamic_inversion.py)
- **Limitations:** The analytical inverse-power gradient sources are inferred and are not reconstructed from measured coil or EPM field maps; the implementation therefore validates mechanism and trends, not the published concentration rate. The model is two-dimensional, dilute, overdamped, and noninteracting; it omits aggregation, rod flexibility, walls beyond rectangular reflection, tissue adhesion, vascular branching, collisions, and fluid-structure coupling. The finite internal-relaxation option is a phenomenological moment-angle relaxation, not a microscopic Neel/domain model. Tirado fitted end corrections are extrapolated above aspect ratio 30. EPM-only waveform fidelity defaults to infeasible because retained-state programming transients are not calibrated as therapeutic polarize/gradient pulses. Hybrid EPM bias/shaping does not yet synthesize a specific 72-element state or include its static force perturbation. Energy and average power remain unavailable unless architecture-specific coil and EPM pulse energies are supplied.

### PEEC coil impedance and parasitics

- **Claim:** PEEC inductance/resistance trends agree with analytical kernels and selected independent QOIL, FastHenry, and FasterCap comparisons.
- **Evidence:** C, A (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Partial-element analytical kernels, bundled QOIL regression values, and optional live external-solver comparisons.
- **Tested range:** Round-wire loops and compact solenoids represented by the bundled test geometries.
- **Metric:** Inductance, resistance, capacitance, and impedance deviation
- **Tolerance:** Tool- and discretization-specific thresholds declared in PEEC tests.
- **References:** QOIL; FastHenry; FasterCap
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_coil_peec.py::test_coil_properties_peec_fields_and_helpers`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_coil_peec.py#L684); [`tests/test_coil_peec_fasthenry.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_coil_peec_fasthenry.py); [`tests/test_coil_peec_fastercap.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_coil_peec_fastercap.py)
- **Limitations:** Live external-tool tests are optional and not run in ordinary CI. Validation is sparse for shields, complex windings, and high-frequency radiation.

### Coupled receiver networks, resonant cancellation, active LNAs, and passive interconnects

- **Claim:** Loaded sensitivity, passive noise covariance, shared-capacitor cancellation, separated active-LNA noise, and reciprocal two-port interconnects reduce to analytical multiport and Friis limits while mutual resistance remains after mutual reactance is cancelled.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Exact two-loop mesh equations, fluctuation-dissipation noise covariance, active one-port voltage/current/cross-noise identities, reciprocal ABCD transformations, the matched-line Friis limit, single-frequency solver agreement, and passive-matrix invariants.
- **Tested range:** Reciprocal passive terminal-impedance matrices with two or more ports; independent per-channel reciprocal passive two-ports; analytical two-loop and matched-line cases near 1-2 MHz; and a compact two-solenoid PEEC example.
- **Metric:** Residual mutual reactance, induced-current isolation, transformed coil-port load, voltage transfer, separated output-noise covariance, insertion loss/noise figure, optimal array SNR, and noise correlation
- **Tolerance:** Machine-precision analytical identities and per-test numerical tolerances; the PEEC geometry, sample-loss values, interconnect, and LNA values are illustrative rather than experimentally calibrated.
- **References:** Hoult and Richards, Journal of Magnetic Resonance 24 (1976), 71-85, DOI 10.1016/0022-2364(76)90233-X; Roemer et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 16 (1990), 192-225, DOI 10.1002/mrm.1910160203; Wang et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 89 (2023), 859-871, DOI 10.1002/mrm.29489; Sun et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 90 (2023), 2198-2210, DOI 10.1002/mrm.29755
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_receiver_network.py::test_shared_capacitor_cancels_mutual_reactance_but_not_resistance`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_receiver_network.py#L398); [`tests/test_receiver_network.py::test_shared_capacitor_mesh_orientation_and_loss_are_physical`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_receiver_network.py#L412); [`tests/test_receiver_frontend.py::test_lossy_matched_line_obeys_friis_noise_limit`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_receiver_frontend.py#L53); [`tests/test_receiver_frontend.py::test_front_end_sweep_reports_preamplifier_decoupling`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_receiver_frontend.py#L85); [`examples/plot_receiver_resonant_cancellation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_receiver_resonant_cancellation.py); [`examples/plot_receiver_lna_architectures.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_receiver_lna_architectures.py); [`examples/plot_receiver_preamplifier_decoupling.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_receiver_preamplifier_decoupling.py)
- **Limitations:** The passive cancellation and interconnect sweeps remain uniform-temperature terminal models. Passive front ends are independent per-channel reciprocal two-ports; coupled transmission lines and measured S-parameter import are pending. The active model separates diagonal LNA R-X||C loading, voltage/current/cross noise, gain, and downstream noise, but standard noise-parameter conversion, cross-channel amplifier noise, stability, compression, and direct Experiment integration remain pending. The sample-loss matrices, conductor geometry, cable, and LNA values are illustrative, with no scanner or bench comparison yet. Cancellation removes mutual reactance at one frequency but not mutual resistance or sensitivity to loading and tolerances; transformed low input impedance can improve isolation without providing a noise match.

### Prescribed-current birdcage geometry and quadrature fields

- **Claim:** Explicit rung and end-ring branch currents satisfy KCL; the ideal fundamental cosine and sine modes are center-field degenerate and orthogonal; and their quadrature combinations select opposite B1 circular components with convergent central-field and ROI metrics.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Discrete end-ring KCL identities, sinusoidal mode orthogonality, finite-segment Biot-Savart superposition, the package B1+/B1- convention, mode-handedness reversal, and end-ring segmentation convergence.
- **Tested range:** Cylindrical cages with at least four rungs; tested reference geometry has 16 rungs, 0.15 m radius, 0.30 m length, fundamental m=1 modes, 4-16 chords per end-ring section, and a central midplane ROI through 40 percent of the cage radius.
- **Metric:** KCL residual, center-field mode degeneracy and inner product, desired/counter-rotating B1 ratio, coefficient of variation, peak-to-peak nonuniformity, transverse fraction, and segmentation convergence
- **Tolerance:** KCL below 1e-12 A; center degeneracy and orthogonality at numerical precision; central-ROI coefficient of variation below 1 percent, peak-to-peak nonuniformity below 3 percent, circular isolation above 40 dB, and 4-versus-16-section center B1 agreement within 5e-4 relative.
- **References:** Hayes et al., Journal of Magnetic Resonance 63 (1985), 622-628, DOI 10.1016/0022-2364(85)90257-4; Jin, Electromagnetic Analysis and Design in Magnetic Resonance Imaging, CRC Press (1999)
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_birdcage.py::test_prescribed_mode_enforces_end_ring_kcl`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_birdcage.py#L44); [`tests/test_birdcage.py::test_fundamental_linear_modes_are_degenerate_and_orthogonal_at_center`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_birdcage.py#L58); [`tests/test_birdcage.py::test_quadrature_modes_select_opposite_circular_components`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_birdcage.py#L80); [`tests/test_birdcage.py::test_quadrature_field_is_uniform_and_circular_in_central_roi`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_birdcage.py#L103); [`tests/test_birdcage.py::test_end_ring_segmentation_converges_at_center`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_birdcage.py#L127); [`examples/plot_birdcage_quadrature.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_birdcage_quadrature.py)
- **Limitations:** This layer prescribes ideal branch currents and does not solve capacitor placement, resonance frequency, port matching, loaded Q, conductor/sample loss, mode splitting, or component tolerances. The field model uses free-space filamentary Biot-Savart segments without shields, dielectric loading, radiation, or measured-coil comparison. Only the fundamental reference geometry and central midplane ROI have quantitative regression thresholds; broader aspect ratios, rung counts, higher modes, and three-dimensional ROIs remain to be validated.

### Thermal networks, conduction, and electromagnets

- **Claim:** Lumped, one-dimensional, axisymmetric, perfused, and advective thermal models reproduce closed-form limits; coupled electromagnets recover exact RL and electrothermal fixed points, and selected conduction cases are cross-checked with FEMM.
- **Evidence:** A, C (validated)
- **Basis:** RC and RL exponential responses, electrothermal fixed points, slab/cylinder/sphere source solutions, conservation laws, advection-diffusion solutions, and FEMM scripts.
- **Tested range:** Constant-property thermal materials, temperature-dependent conductor resistance, standard boundary conditions, and selected coupled coil/sample/electromagnet cases.
- **Metric:** Temperature, current, B0, energy balance, steady-state rise, and transient time constant
- **Tolerance:** Analytical solver/discretization tolerances declared per test and FEMM validation script.
- **References:** FEMM; Classical heat-equation and Pennes limits
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_thermal.py::test_single_node_exponential_transient`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_thermal.py#L211); [`tests/test_thermal.py::test_slab_uniform_source_parabola`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_thermal.py#L496); [`tests/test_thermal.py::test_advection_diffusion_matches_analytic`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_thermal.py#L650); [`tests/test_electrothermal_electromagnet.py::test_voltage_step_matches_exact_rl_response_when_resistance_is_constant`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electrothermal_electromagnet.py#L35); [`tests/test_electrothermal_electromagnet.py::test_constant_voltage_reaches_coupled_electrothermal_fixed_point`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_electrothermal_electromagnet.py#L53); [`validation/femm/validate_conduction.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/validation/femm/validate_conduction.py)
- **Limitations:** No general full-3D or CFD thermal validation. Electromagnet validation is analytical and does not cover nonlinear ferromagnetic cores or measured supply/sensor dynamics.

### NQR Hamiltonians and pulse models

- **Claim:** Spin-1 and spin-3/2 transition conventions, powder weights, selective pulses, and SORC/SLSE limits reproduce analytical and published theory results.
- **Evidence:** A, D (partially validated)

- **Tested range:** Spin 1 and 3/2 core cases, axial/asymmetric EFGs, single-crystal and powder grids, and weak-B0 limits.
- **Metric:** Frequency, population transfer, normalized powder signal, and operator identities
- **Tolerance:** Analytical numerical tolerances declared per test; published-example agreement at reported precision.
- **References:** Konnai SORC powder theory; Glickstein spin-1 polarization enhancement example

- **Limitations:** Experimental waveform and absolute-signal comparisons remain limited. Higher-spin validation is primarily analytical rather than experimental.

### ESR/EPR spectra and pulsed dynamics

- **Claim:** Zeeman resonance, lineshape, hyperfine splitting, relaxation, and Hahn-echo behavior reproduce analytical spin-1/2 limits.
- **Evidence:** A, D (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Bohr-magneton resonance, Hermiticity/scaling identities, exact isotropic hyperfine doublets, and echo-refocusing theory.
- **Tested range:** Single-electron spin-1/2 systems with scalar/anisotropic g, simple hyperfine systems, static disorder, and phenomenological T1/T2.

- **Limitations:** No broad experimental spectral library comparison. Multi-electron and general anisotropic hyperfine systems remain incomplete.

### Small scalar-coupled spin systems

- **Claim:** Dense spin operators, scalar-coupling Hamiltonians, and selected low-field editing models satisfy exact operator and spectral limits.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Commutators, Hermiticity, trace conservation, exact two-spin energy levels, and synthetic editing limits.
- **Tested range:** Small dense spin-1/2 systems and the implemented J-editing/TANGO/SLIC models.
- **Metric:** Operator identities, eigenvalues, populations, and filter response
- **Tolerance:** Near floating-point precision for algebraic identities.

- **Limitations:** Paper-level fixtures and relaxation-aware general pulse-sequence comparisons are still sparse.

### Singlet, triplet, and parahydrogen state primitives

- **Claim:** Embedded spin-pair singlet/triplet projectors, swap symmetry, singlet-order observables, and para/ortho hydrogen mixtures satisfy exact spin-1/2 algebra and physical density-matrix limits.
- **Evidence:** A, R (validated)
- **Basis:** Exact singlet/triplet projector identities, pair-permutation eigenvalues, trace and positivity constraints, and the para-H2 statistical-mixture identity rho=I/4+(f_p-1/4)Q_S.
- **Tested range:** Spin-1/2 pairs embedded in two- and three-spin systems; para fractions from 0 to 1.
- **Metric:** Hermiticity, idempotence, orthogonality, completeness, trace, eigenvalues, population, and singlet-order amplitude
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point algebraic tolerance of 1e-10 or tighter.
- **References:** Carravetta and Levitt, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 126 (2004) 6228-6229, doi:10.1021/ja0490931; DeVience, Walsworth, and Rosen, arXiv:1307.0832
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_hyperpolarization_singlet.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_hyperpolarization_singlet.py); [`tests/test_coupling.py::test_two_spin_slic_matching_and_transfer_roles_are_distinct`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_coupling.py#L101); [`tests/test_coupling.py::test_exactly_equivalent_pair_has_no_slic_transfer`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_coupling.py#L108); [`examples/singlet_parahydrogen_states.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/singlet_parahydrogen_states.py)
- **Limitations:** This record validates state algebra and ideal SLIC limits; workflow-level LLS and PHIP invariants are tracked separately.

### Long-lived singlet and hydrogenative PHIP reference workflows

- **Claim:** SLIC preparation/storage/readout obeys its analytical matching and exponential T_S limits, while hydrogenative product order is physical and linear in para excess and pairwise-addition fraction.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Exact dense two-spin propagation, trace and positivity checks, analytical singlet-mode exponential decay, product-state normalization, and linear PHIP source-order scaling.
- **Tested range:** Nearly equivalent two-proton SLIC pair; physical and deviation storage densities; two- and three-spin product mappings; para fractions from 0.25 to 1; pairwise fractions from 0 to 1; high-field PASADENA and explicit piecewise ALTADENA trajectories.
- **Metric:** Prepared singlet amplitude, normalized readout decay, trace, minimum density eigenvalue, PHIP FID amplitude, and linear scaling residual
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point invariant tolerance of 1e-10; ideal SLIC preparation amplitude within 0.002 of unity.
- **References:** DeVience, Walsworth, and Rosen, arXiv:1307.0832; Cavallari et al., Frontiers in Oncology 11, 617307 (2021), doi:10.3389/fonc.2021.617307
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_hyperpolarization_workflows.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_hyperpolarization_workflows.py); [`examples/plot_lls_phip_workflows.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_lls_phip_workflows.py)
- **Limitations:** T_S is a measured phenomenological input rather than a microscopic correlated-relaxation prediction. Pairwise hydrogenation yield, catalyst chemistry, reaction-time distributions, and scrambling are external inputs or not yet modeled. PASADENA and ALTADENA currently have algebraic and regression validation only; published spectral fixtures and PH-INEPT transfer remain to be added.

### Phenomenological and Redfield relaxation

- **Claim:** Relaxation propagators preserve required invariants and limiting behavior; measured weak-field 35Cl SLSE relaxation is reproduced; the non-diagonal zero-field Redfield model reproduces published transition-resolved 209Bi FVA rate shapes; and RDX NMR/NQR observations recover the published activated barrier and cross-relaxation assignments.
- **Evidence:** A, D, E, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Trace/Hermiticity preservation, equilibrium limits, Chen et al. Table 1 measurements, 24 experimental plus published FA/FVA rates from Goesweiner et al. Table 1, Smith et al. RDX Figures 2 and 8, and a read-only audit of 89 NQRDatabase relaxation records.
- **Tested range:** Implemented Bloch, Liouville, BPP/Redfield, wall, and rotating-frame models; NaClO3 powder from 0 to 41 G; three 209Bi aryl compounds at 77 and 310 K with four transitions each; RDX 14N NQR from 266 to 340 K and 1H cross-relaxation minima from 0 to 540 kHz.
- **Metric:** Invariant diagnostics, experimental RMS rate residual, coupled/diagonal lowest-transition ratio, mean relative FVA rate-shape deviation, Arrhenius activation energy, and cross-relaxation resonance position
- **Tolerance:** NaClO3 RMS residual <= 10 s^-1 and nonzero-field T2 within 15%; 209Bi mean relative deviation from published FVA rate shapes < 10% after one amplitude scale per sample/temperature group; RDX activation energy within 4 kJ/mol of 92 kJ/mol and resonance centers within 10 kHz.
- **References:** Bloch exponential relaxation; BPP and Redfield limiting formulas; Chen et al., J. Magn. Reson. 311, 106660 (2020), doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2019.106660; Goesweiner et al., Molecular Physics 118, e1743888 (2020), doi:10.1080/00268976.2020.1743888; Smith et al., J. Magn. Reson. 213, 98-106 (2011), doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2011.09.011
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_relaxation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_relaxation.py); [`tests/test_relaxation_workflows.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_relaxation_workflows.py); [`tests/test_nqr_redfield_relaxation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_nqr_redfield_relaxation.py); [`tests/test_relaxation_validation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_relaxation_validation.py); [`tests/test_nqr_database_relaxation_audit.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_nqr_database_relaxation_audit.py); [`validation/audit_nqr_relaxation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/validation/audit_nqr_relaxation.py); [`examples/plot_chen2020_slse_relaxation.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_chen2020_slse_relaxation.py); [`examples/plot_quadrupolar_relaxation_workflow.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_quadrupolar_relaxation_workflow.py); [`examples/plot_field_cycling_nmrd.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_field_cycling_nmrd.py)
- **Limitations:** The NaClO3 field-independent floor and absolute cross-relaxation strength are fitted nuisance parameters. The 209Bi validation fits one amplitude normalization per material/temperature group and is uneven for tris(4-fluorophenyl)bismuth at 77 K, where the published single-mode FVA model is also inaccurate. RDX values are figure-digitized; differing sample preparations preclude a joint absolute-amplitude fit, and the full heteronuclear dispersion model is not yet implemented. NQRDatabase has no immediately fit-eligible microscopic relaxation series and contains a factor-1000 sodium-nitrite source conflict.

### ENDOR-QDyne coherent basis mapping and linewidth

- **Claim:** The resolved-spin ENDOR-QDyne model reproduces the ideal coherent-basis-mapping signal, phase-cycled carrier, weak-measurement back-action map, initialization-infidelity linewidth, and proof-of-principle timing reported by Meinel et al.
- **Evidence:** A, D, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Main-text Eqs. 1-3, Supplementary Eqs. 14 and 23, the reported operation timings, and direct deterministic regressions against the corresponding closed-form expressions.
- **Tested range:** Spin-one-half target; finite signed longitudinal Azz coupling in Hz; configurable RF reference, free-precession and sensing intervals, RF phase cycling, residual sensing phase, clock errors, sensor T2*, intrinsic nuclear decay, initialization fidelity, optional optical counts, and exact or disabled weak-measurement back-action; paper preset at Azz=6 kHz and 105.5 us repetition.
- **Metric:** Samplewise Iz and Sz expectation values, RF operation and total cycle time, baseband carrier and FFT peak, exact and leading initialization decay rates, and discrete back-action recurrence.
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point agreement for analytical identities; less than one Fourier bin for the simulated carrier; within 2 Hz of the reported 2.368 kHz phase-cycle target; the approximately 1 kHz Eq. 3 numerical estimate is reproduced as 1.012 kHz using the paper's 2*pi*Azz*Sz*Iz Hamiltonian and spectroscopic-Hz convention.
- **References:** J. Meinel et al., Communications Physics 6 (2023) 302, doi:10.1038/s42005-023-01419-2; Supplementary Information for High-resolution nanoscale NMR for arbitrary magnetic fields, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-2826442/v1
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_nano_mr_endor_qdyne.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_nano_mr_endor_qdyne.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_endor_qdyne.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_endor_qdyne.py)
- **Limitations:** The comparison uses the authors' published equations, sequence timings, and reported carrier/linewidth targets rather than a refit of deposited raw photon-count traces. The source's nearby statement Azz*tau=0.63 rad omits the 2*pi conversion implied by its Hamiltonian and approximately 1 kHz estimate; the implementation explicitly treats Azz as a cyclic frequency in Hz. RF basis mapping is ideal apart from an explicit residual sensing phase; off-resonant finite-pulse unitary errors, charge-state switching, excited-state hyperfine changes, and a microscopic optical reset channel are not propagated. The model covers one resolved spin-one-half target and an effective optical readout, not a many-spin ENDOR ensemble or a calibrated high-field instrument.

### Defect-spin nanoscale spectroscopy, MRI, and package integration

- **Claim:** Implemented defect, bath, control, optical, statistical, exact-cluster, motion, imaging, high-resolution, and facade layers satisfy their documented analytical identities and deterministic/seeded regression contracts.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Spin-Hamiltonian eigenvalue and rotational-covariance identities; inverse-cube dipolar and layer-depth laws; sequence/filter integrals; polarization, Lorentzian normalization, Brownian MSD/drift/confinement and propagator-tail references, optical-count preparation/transfer, Qdyne visibility/alias/bin, memory-envelope, chemical-shift/J, and DNP limits; plus facade/direct delegation, config/archive round trips, Bayesian binding, and complexity gates.
- **Tested range:** Built-in diamond NV-minus and configurable 4H-SiC PL6 presets; supported isotope presets; uniform/voxel baths; small dense resolved clusters; seeded three-dimensional trajectories; scanning/array forward models; effective optical/SPAD models; coherent clocked tones; analytic planar statistical spectra; compact Qdyne facade experiments.
- **Metric:** Eigenvalues, tensor scaling/covariance, PSD integral and peak position, coherence, moments, photon-count statistics, reconstruction error, recovered beat/bin spacing, envelope decomposition, multiplet positions, polarization limits, facade result/config identity, planner feasibility, work units, memory, and loose wall time.
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point, seeded-statistical, reconstruction, and deliberately loose performance tolerances declared in tests.
- **References:** C. L. Degen, F. Reinhard, and P. Cappellaro, Reviews of Modern Physics 89 (2017) 035002, doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.89.035002; S. Schmitt et al., Science 356 (2017) 832-837, doi:10.1126/science.aam5532; J. M. Boss et al., Science 356 (2017) 837-840, doi:10.1126/science.aam7009
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_nano_mr.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_nano_mr.py); [`tests/test_nano_mr_experiment.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_nano_mr_experiment.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_statistical_spectra.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_statistical_spectra.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_diffusing_liquid.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_diffusing_liquid.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_scan_reconstruction.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_scan_reconstruction.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_realistic_noise.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_realistic_noise.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_qdyne.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_qdyne.py); [`examples/plot_nano_mr_chemical_shift_j.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/plot_nano_mr_chemical_shift_j.py); [`examples/nano_mr_experiment_facade.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/nano_mr_experiment_facade.py); [`examples/bayesian_design_nano_mr_qdyne.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/examples/bayesian_design_nano_mr_qdyne.py)
- **Limitations:** The current evidence is analytical and synthetic regression evidence; it does not compare predictions with a calibrated NV, SiC, optical, or scanning experiment. Defect and detector parameters are configurable phenomenology rather than ab initio or device-specific calibration, and the Phase-8 facade covers planar statistical spectra and coherent Qdyne rather than every expert nano-MR backend. The Qdyne facade signal is a coherent classical tone; it does not make a statistically polarized nanoscale bath phase coherent. The Gaussian return-propagator tail is an analytic reference, not an end-to-end convergence validation of trajectory-derived dipolar correlations. Exact clusters remain small dense systems, and coherent chemical-shift/J and DNP models are effective first-order descriptions.

### Reproducible results and provenance

- **Claim:** Facade archives identify experiment inputs, implementation, numerical environment, randomness, and result content and can verify an exact rerun while remaining backward-compatible with version-1 archives.
- **Evidence:** R (regression only)
- **Basis:** Canonical fingerprint invariance/change tests, archive integrity checks, seeded/unseeded classification, exact rerun comparison, CLI verification, and legacy archive loading.
- **Tested range:** Deterministic and noisy facade runs, NPZ format versions 1 and 2.
- **Metric:** SHA-256 identity equality and structured reproduction verdict
- **Tolerance:** Exact canonical metadata and result bytes.
- **References:** FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_provenance_fingerprints_are_stable_and_specific`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L157); [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_provenance_classifies_seeded_and_unseeded_randomness`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L194); [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_version_one_run_archive_remains_readable`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L211); [`tests/test_experiment.py::test_archive_fingerprints_detect_spec_and_result_tampering`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment.py#L243); [`tests/test_experiment_cli.py::test_cli_run_and_show`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_experiment_cli.py#L212)
- **Limitations:** Exact computational reproduction does not validate the physical model; unseeded legacy runs cannot be made reproducible after the fact.

### Bayesian experiment design and adaptive acquisition

- **Claim:** Bayesian updates, goal utilities, planner-validated adapters, batched PGSE parity, surrogate validation, staged/adaptive scoring, paired end-to-end adapter benchmarks, recoverable live batches, discrete-target nuisance marginalization, and robustness diagnostics follow their stated numerical and decision-theory contracts.
- **Evidence:** A, R (partially validated)
- **Basis:** Direct Bayes-rule and dense mutual-information calculations, prior-predictive coverage, deterministic replay, facade binding tests, paired common-truth/common-noise adaptive-versus-fixed trials for every Phase 2 adapter, exact prediction-table identity checks, batched-vs-facade PGSE parity, atomic checkpoint replacement, pending-call recovery, complete-outcome validation, rejection exclusion, explicit latency accounting, exact polynomial recovery, held-out surrogate errors, linear-Gaussian screening limits, nuisance-only target-information cancellation, discrepancy variance addition, model dispatch, and recommendation sensitivity cases.
- **Tested range:** Scalar/vector real and complex Gaussian observations; finite Cartesian grids and weighted particles; finite candidate spaces; CPMG-IR, deterministic PGSE, NQR FID, ESR Hahn, and coherent Qdyne adapters; polynomial response surfaces; discrete target/model labels.
- **Metric:** Posterior probability, mutual information, expected variance reduction, credible coverage, ranking and replay identity, planner feasibility, batch parity, atomic recovery identity, accepted/rejected update count, latency budget status, surrogate RMSE/correlation, Monte Carlo sample allocation, mixture dispatch, sensitivity agreement, physical seconds, and measured planning wall time.
- **Tolerance:** Floating-point or Monte Carlo tolerances declared in tests; prior-predictive coverage is required not to under-cover its nominal discrete interval in the fixed-seed reference.
- **References:** T. Rainforth et al., Statistical Science 39 (2024) 100-114, doi:10.1214/23-STS915; C. A. Waudby et al., Journal of Magnetic Resonance 326 (2021) 106937, doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2021.106937
- **Reproduce:** [`tests/test_bayesian_design.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_bayesian_design.py); [`tests/test_bayesian_design_core.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_bayesian_design_core.py); [`tests/test_bayesian_design_adapters.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_bayesian_design_adapters.py); [`tests/test_bayesian_design_performance.py`](https://github.com/supertjhok/MRSpinDynamics/blob/main/PythonSpinDynamics/tests/test_bayesian_design_performance.py);
